description: Specs Viewer/Editor page — a three-panel layout for viewing, editing, and managing project specifications of all types (page specs, architecture, API, data, dependency, constraint). The left panel shows a hierarchical spec tree grouped by application. The center panel shows spec details with inline editing, a tabbed view (Assertions / Issues / Triage) for page specs, and specialized views for other spec types. The right panel provides AI chat for spec review, gap analysis, creation, and workflow building. A connection bar below the header provides buttons to load bundled specs, load/save files, discover specs from running apps via UI Bridge, toggle edit mode, trigger AI eval, run spec sync, check drift, and compile the runtime state machine. The page header offers three view modes: Editor (default), Contracts, and Experimentation.

groups.name: Page Structure and View Modes
groups.description: The Specs page header contains a ShieldCheck icon, the 'Specs' title, a mode badge ('viewer' or 'editor'), and three view-mode toggle buttons on the right: Editor (default), Contracts, and Experimentation. The initial view mode is 'Editor'. Each button activates its mode and the selected button gets a highlighted background.

assertions.description: A heading with text 'Specs' is visible in the page header
A mode badge is visible in the header showing either 'viewer' (default) or 'editor' when edit mode is on
An 'Editor' button is visible in the page header's right area for switching to the main editor view mode
A 'Contracts' button with a FileJson icon is visible in the page header for switching to the contract builder view
An 'Experimentation' button with a FlaskConical icon is visible in the page header for switching to the experimentation dashboard

Clicking 'Contracts' switches the center+right panel area to show the ContractBuilder component. Clicking 'Experimentation' shows the SpecExperimentationDashboard. Clicking 'Editor' returns to the three-panel spec editor layout. The active mode button shows a highlighted zinc-700 background.

groups.name: Connection Bar — Spec Loading Controls
groups.description: Below the page header, the connection bar provides controls for loading specs. 'Bundled' (purple, BookOpen icon) loads all pre-packaged specs shipped with the runner. 'File' (emerald, FolderOpen icon) opens a file dialog to load spec files from disk. A URL input (defaulting to http://localhost:3001) and 'Discover' (cyan, Search icon) button connect to a running application via UI Bridge to discover its specs. These controls are always visible regardless of current spec selection state.

assertions.description: A 'Bundled' button with a BookOpen icon is visible in the connection bar
A 'File' button with a FolderOpen icon is visible in the connection bar
A URL input field with placeholder 'http://localhost:3001' is visible in the connection bar
A 'Discover' button with a Search icon is visible next to the URL input in the connection bar

Clicking 'Bundled' fetches the discovered specs from the runner's Spec API (GET /spec/list), then loads user-persisted specs via the Tauri 'load_user_specs' command. After loading, the spec tree populates with spec nodes grouped by application name, the stats row shows updated counts (N specs / M groups / K assertions), and no spec is automatically selected.

Clicking 'Discover' (or pressing Enter in the URL input) sends a POST to /ui-bridge/sdk/discover-and-cache on the target app, then fetches discovered specs. The connection status row shows a cyan spinner and 'Connecting…' during the request, then either a green checkmark with the app name on success or a red alert with the error message on failure. Discovered specs merge into the tree alongside bundled/file specs.

groups.name: Connection Bar — Spec Action Controls
groups.description: When a spec is selected, additional action buttons appear in the connection bar. 'Edit'/'Done' (amber, Pencil/PencilOff icon) toggles edit mode for page specs. 'Save' (Save icon) exports the selected spec to disk. 'AI Eval' (Brain icon, amber when active) forces all assertions to be AI-evaluated instead of using fast deterministic checks. 'Regression (N)' (Bug icon, purple) appears only when known issues exist and N > 0. 'Generate with AI (spec brief)' (Sparkles, fuchsia when on, id=specs-ai-toggle, role=switch) toggles the AI workflow-generation pipeline. 'Build Workflow'/'Generating…' (orange Hammer/Loader2) builds a verification workflow. 'Sync All Specs' (teal RefreshCw) re-syncs all stale specs with AI. 'Check Drift' (SpecDriftButton) scans source for unspecced elements. 'Compile State Machine' (violet Network) compiles stateMachine sections into the runtime engine.

assertions.description: When a page-spec is selected, an 'Edit' button (Pencil icon) is visible in the connection bar. When edit mode is active, it shows 'Done' with a PencilOff icon styled in amber.
assertions.precondition: A page-spec is selected

assertions.description: A 'Generate with AI (spec brief)' toggle button with id=specs-ai-toggle, role=switch, and aria-pressed attribute is visible in the connection bar. It shows fuchsia styling when aria-pressed=true (default on) and muted styling when aria-pressed=false.
When any spec is selected, a 'Build Workflow' button (orange Hammer) is visible in the connection bar. During AI generation, it shows a Loader2 spinner and 'Generating…' text and is disabled.
assertions.precondition: Any spec is selected

assertions.description: A 'Sync All Specs' button (teal RefreshCw) is visible in the connection bar. It is disabled when no specs are loaded. While syncing it shows 'Syncing N/M...' with a spinning icon and a '(cancel)' label.
A 'Compile State Machine' button (violet Network icon) is visible in the connection bar. It is disabled when no specs are loaded.
When specs are loaded, the right end of the connection bar shows three counts in muted text: 'N specs', 'M groups', 'K assertions'. These update whenever specs are added or removed.

target.label: Stats row (N specs / M groups / K assertions)

assertions.precondition: At least one spec is loaded

groups.name: Connection Status Row
groups.description: A second row below the connection bar buttons appears when the connection status is not 'disconnected'. It shows real-time discovery status: cyan spinner and 'Connecting…' while in flight, green CheckCircle2 and the app name when connected, red AlertCircle and the error message when discovery failed. The row is absent when disconnected.

assertions.description: While discovery is in progress, a status row appears below the connection bar buttons showing a cyan animated Loader2 spinner and the text 'Connecting…'
assertions.precondition: Discover was clicked and the request is in flight

assertions.description: After successful discovery, the status row shows a green CheckCircle2 icon and the connected application's name (e.g., 'qontinui-web')
assertions.precondition: Discovery completed successfully

groups.name: Sync Progress Banner
groups.description: When 'Sync All Specs' is triggered, a teal-tinted banner appears below the connection bar showing real-time sync progress. Phase labels cycle through: 'Analyzing specs…', 'Syncing N+1/M' (with a progress bar and current spec name truncated to 200px), 'Compiling state machine…', and 'Sync complete'. On completion the banner shows counts: green 'N updated' (CheckCircle2), muted 'M skipped', optional red 'K failed' (AlertTriangle), optional amber 'J warnings'. An X button cancels in-progress syncs or dismisses the completed banner.

assertions.description: After clicking 'Sync All Specs', a teal-tinted banner appears below the connection bar showing 'Analyzing specs…' in teal text
assertions.precondition: Sync All Specs was clicked with at least one spec loaded

assertions.description: When sync completes, the banner shows 'Sync complete' and a summary row with green 'N updated', muted 'M skipped', optional red 'K failed', optional amber 'J warnings' counts. The X button dismisses the banner.
assertions.precondition: Sync has completed

assertions.description: Sync All Specs re-runs the AI against every loaded spec whose structure is stale (missing stateMachine section, or groups that don't align with current states). The AI-regenerated output is merged back into the in-memory spec. Up-to-date specs are skipped. After syncing, the spec tree reflects updated group/assertion counts. Clicking X mid-sync cancels remaining specs without rolling back already-updated ones.
assertions.precondition: At least one spec is loaded

groups.name: Spec Tree — Navigation Sidebar
groups.description: The left sidebar shows a hierarchical tree of all loaded specs under a 'Specifications' heading. Specs are grouped by application name when specs from multiple apps are loaded. Each node shows a type-specific icon (Shield for page-spec, Server for architecture, Globe for API, Database for data, GitBranch for dependency, Gauge for constraint), a truncated label, and a child-item count in muted text. Page specs expand via a ChevronRight/ChevronDown chevron to show child group nodes. data-ui-id attributes follow the pattern 'spec-tree-{specId}'.

assertions.description: The spec tree sidebar shows a 'Specifications' heading above the tree nodes
When no specs are loaded, the tree shows a 'No specs loaded.' message with guidance to load bundled specs or connect to an app
assertions.precondition: No specs have been loaded

assertions.description: Clicking a spec node in the tree selects it (node gets highlight styling) and the center detail panel updates immediately. Clicking a child group node navigates directly to the GroupDetail view. Clicking a spec node when a group was selected navigates back to the spec overview.
assertions.precondition: At least one spec is loaded

assertions.description: Page spec nodes with groups show a ChevronRight icon that rotates to ChevronDown when expanded, revealing indented child group nodes. Clicking the chevron toggles expansion without changing the selection. Clicking a spec node both selects it and expands it if it has children.
assertions.precondition: A page spec with groups is loaded

assertions.description: Specs are organized into three sources: bundled (from the runner's spec registry), discovered (from a connected app via UI Bridge), and file (loaded from disk). Within each source, specs are grouped by appName. User-persisted specs override their bundled counterparts. The tree order is: bundled runner specs first, then bundled web specs, then discovered specs, then file specs.
assertions.precondition: Bundled specs are loaded

groups.name: Detail Panel — No Selection
groups.description: When no spec is selected, the center detail panel renders the GlobalIssuesPanel component. When an unspecced-page node is selected, a centered view appears with an amber Shield icon, the page label as a heading, the expected spec ID in a code element (amber text), and a 'Generate Spec' button (purple Plus icon) that triggers AI spec creation.

assertions.description: When an unspecced-page node is selected, a 'Generate Spec' button is visible in the center panel with a Plus icon
assertions.precondition: An unspecced-page node is selected

assertions.description: Clicking 'Generate Spec' for an unspecced page triggers AI-driven spec creation: it sets a generateSpecRequest with the page's expectedSpecId, label, and description. The SpecChatPanel receives this request and sends an automatic creation prompt to the AI. The resulting spec JSON, when applied via the 'Apply as spec' button, adds the new spec to the tree with the expected spec ID and auto-selects it.
assertions.precondition: An unspecced-page node is selected

groups.name: Detail Panel — Page Spec Tabs (Assertions / Issues / Triage)
groups.description: When a page-spec is selected at the spec level (not a group), the center panel shows three tabs: 'Assertions' (Shield icon, default active) renders PageSpecOverview. 'Issues' (Bug icon) renders SpecIssuesPanel showing known issues filtered by specId and pageUrl. 'Triage' (AlertTriangle icon) renders SpecTriageView for regression triage. The active tab has a highlighted border-b-0 rounded-t style. Tab state is local to SpecDetailPanel and resets when a new spec is selected.

assertions.description: When a page-spec is selected, an 'Assertions' tab with a Shield icon is visible at the top of the detail panel and is active by default (highlighted)
assertions.precondition: A page-spec is selected at the spec level

assertions.description: An 'Issues' tab with a Bug icon is visible next to the Assertions tab in the detail panel
assertions.precondition: A page-spec is selected at the spec level

assertions.description: A 'Triage' tab with an AlertTriangle icon is visible next to the Issues tab in the detail panel
assertions.precondition: A page-spec is selected at the spec level

assertions.description: Clicking 'Issues' replaces PageSpecOverview with SpecIssuesPanel showing known issues for the selected spec. Clicking 'Triage' shows SpecTriageView. Clicking 'Assertions' returns to PageSpecOverview. The active tab gains highlighted border-b-0 styling; inactive tabs are transparent with hover underline.
assertions.precondition: A page-spec is selected at the spec level

groups.name: Detail Panel — Page Spec Overview (Assertions Tab)
groups.description: The Assertions tab for a selected page-spec renders PageSpecOverview: the spec ID as a heading, description text, a 'Categories' section listing unique assertion categories used, and a 'Groups' section listing all groups. Each group row shows its category badge, name, and enabled assertion count. Clicking a group row navigates to GroupDetail for that group. In edit mode, groups show trash icons and an 'Add group' form appears at the bottom.

assertions.description: A 'Groups' section is visible in the spec overview, listing all groups with their category badge, name, and enabled assertion count
assertions.precondition: A page-spec with at least one group is selected on the Assertions tab

assertions.description: A 'Categories' section is visible listing all unique assertion categories used in the spec (e.g., 'element-presence', 'semantic', 'behavior', 'state-consistency')
assertions.precondition: A page-spec is selected on the Assertions tab

assertions.description: Clicking a group row in the spec overview navigates to that group's GroupDetail view in the center panel. The navigation is equivalent to clicking the group node in the spec tree.
assertions.precondition: A page-spec with at least one group is selected on the Assertions tab

groups.name: Detail Panel — Group Detail View
groups.description: When a group node is selected, the center panel shows GroupDetail: the group name as a heading with a category badge, the group description, and a scrollable list of all assertions. Each assertion row shows a severity badge (red=critical, yellow=warning, blue=info), eye icon for enabled state (full opacity=enabled, dimmed=disabled), description text, assertionType badge, category badge, and source badge. A precondition tag appears when set. In edit mode, eye icons are clickable and trash icons appear.

assertions.description: Each assertion in the group is rendered as a row showing a color-coded severity badge, enabled eye icon, description text, assertionType badge, category badge, and source badge

target.label: Assertion severity badge in group detail

assertions.precondition: A group with at least one assertion is selected

assertions.description: A well-formed group contains a mix of deterministic assertion types (exists, visible, hasText, count, enabled) for static UI state checks AND semantic types (behavior, semantic) for interaction results and data logic. A group containing only 'exists' assertions is incomplete — it verifies elements are present but not that they work. The type badges in each assertion row reveal this mix visually.
assertions.precondition: A group with multiple assertions is selected

groups.name: Edit Mode — Inline Assertion and Group Management
groups.description: Edit mode is activated by clicking 'Edit' in the connection bar (only available for page-spec selections). The mode badge changes from 'viewer' to 'editor', and the Edit button shows 'Done' in amber. In group detail: eye icons become clickable toggles, trash icons appear on each assertion, and an 'Add assertion' button reveals an inline form. In spec overview: group rows show trash icons and an 'Add group' button reveals a creation form. Clicking 'Done' exits edit mode.

assertions.description: When edit mode is active, the mode badge in the header shows 'editor' instead of 'viewer'
assertions.precondition: Edit mode is active

assertions.description: In edit mode on a group detail view, clicking the eye icon on an assertion immediately toggles its enabled state. The eye changes between full-opacity (enabled) and dimmed/strikethrough styling (disabled). The change is reflected in the spec state in memory and persisted to the user store via the Tauri 'save_page_spec' command if the spec is user-owned.

target.label: Assertion eye toggle in edit mode

assertions.precondition: Edit mode is active and a group is selected

assertions.description: In edit mode on a group detail, an 'Add assertion' button is visible. Clicking it reveals an inline form with a description textarea and severity dropdown (critical/warning/info). Submitting appends a new assertion with assertionType='exists', source='manual', enabled=true, and the entered description/severity. The form closes after submission.
assertions.precondition: Edit mode is active and a group is selected

assertions.description: In edit mode on the spec overview (Assertions tab), an 'Add group' button is visible. Clicking it reveals a form with name (text input), category (dropdown), and description (textarea) fields. Submitting appends a new empty group to the spec. The new group appears immediately in both the tree and the overview.
assertions.precondition: Edit mode is active and a page-spec is selected at the spec overview level

groups.name: AI Chat Panel
groups.description: The right panel is the AI Chat interface. It shows an 'AI Chat' heading, a scrollable message history, a textarea input, and a send/stop button. User messages show a cyan User icon in a small circle with cyan-tinted background. AI responses show a purple Bot icon with dark background and full markdown rendering (code blocks, lists, inline code). System messages appear centered in italic muted text. A session status indicator and a 'New' button reset the session and clear history. When the AI generates a spec JSON in a ```json block, an 'Apply as [type] spec' button appears below the message with data-testid='apply-{kind}-{specId}'.

assertions.description: An 'AI Chat' heading is visible at the top of the right panel
A 'New' button is visible in the chat panel header for resetting the AI session and clearing message history

When the AI response contains a valid spec JSON in a ```json code block whose content matches a spec schema (has 'groups' array, 'version', etc.), a green 'Apply as [type] spec' button appears below the message. Clicking it parses the JSON, derives the SpecKind from structure, adds the spec to the tree, and auto-selects it. The button data-testid follows the pattern 'apply-{kind}-{specId}' with colons/slashes replaced by hyphens.
assertions.precondition: The AI has responded with a message containing a valid spec JSON code block

assertions.description: When a spec is selected and the user sends a message, the spec's full formatted context (built by buildDetailedSpecContext — includes spec ID, description, all group names/categories, assertion types and descriptions) is prepended to the AI session as system context. This occurs automatically without user intervention. System context messages appear in the chat as centered italic muted text.
assertions.precondition: A spec is selected and a message has been sent

groups.name: AI Chat — Review and Create Modes
groups.description: The chat panel has two toggle modes: 'Review' and 'Create'. In Review mode, four quick-action buttons appear ('Review spec quality', 'Find gaps', 'Suggest improvements', 'Generate assertions'), and for page specs a 'Build verification workflow' button (Hammer) also appears. In Create mode, template buttons appear ('New Page Spec', 'New Architecture Spec', 'New API Spec', 'New Data Spec'). The modes are mutually exclusive toggles — clicking the active mode's button deactivates it. Input placeholder text reflects the active mode.

assertions.description: A 'Review' toggle button is visible in the AI chat panel
A 'Create' toggle button is visible in the AI chat panel

When Review mode is active, four quick-action buttons appear: 'Review spec quality', 'Find gaps', 'Suggest improvements', 'Generate assertions'. Clicking any immediately populates the chat input with a predefined prompt and sends it, triggering an AI response in the chat.
assertions.precondition: Review mode is active

assertions.description: In review mode with a page-spec selected, a 'Build verification workflow' button (Hammer icon) is visible in the quick actions area. Clicking it triggers the same workflow-building pipeline as the connection bar 'Build Workflow' button.
assertions.precondition: Review mode is active and a page-spec is selected

assertions.description: When Create mode is active, template buttons appear: 'New Page Spec', 'New Architecture Spec', 'New API Spec', 'New Data Spec'. Clicking any sends a creation prompt instructing the AI to generate a complete spec JSON of the requested type in a code block. The resulting response contains an 'Apply as [type] spec' button.
assertions.precondition: Create mode is active

groups.name: Build Workflow Pipeline
groups.description: The 'Build Workflow' button triggers workflow generation from the selected spec. Two paths exist: AI path (toggle on, default) calls buildSpecBrief() → generateFromBrief() to produce a richer workflow with setup/navigation steps; deterministic path (toggle off) calls buildSpecWorkflow() for a straightforward assertion verification workflow. For non-page specs, the workflow embeds the full spec JSON as an agentic step prompt. All workflows are POSTed to /unified-workflows with category='spec-generated' and tags=['spec','auto-generated'], then the user is navigated to the workflow builder tab.

assertions.description: With the AI toggle on, clicking 'Build Workflow' shows 'Generating…' on the button (Loader2 spinner, disabled) until the pipeline completes. On success, the user is navigated to the workflow builder with the new workflow selected. The workflow has category='spec-generated', tags=['spec','auto-generated'], and includes setup steps for page navigation alongside assertion verification steps.
assertions.precondition: A page-spec is selected and AI toggle is on (aria-pressed=true)

assertions.description: With the AI toggle off, clicking 'Build Workflow' synchronously calls buildSpecWorkflow() to create assertion verification steps, POSTs to /unified-workflows, and navigates to the builder. No 'Generating…' loading state is shown because the deterministic path is fast.
assertions.precondition: A page-spec is selected and AI toggle is off (aria-pressed=false)

assertions.description: Building a workflow from a non-page spec (architecture, API, data, dependency, constraint) generates a prompt-based workflow: a single agentic step that embeds the full spec JSON as verification context rather than individual assertion steps. The AI interprets the spec to determine verification criteria.
assertions.precondition: A non-page spec is selected (architecture/api/data/dependency/constraint)

groups.name: Spec Drift Detection
groups.description: The SpecDriftButton in the connection bar invokes the Tauri 'scan_spec_drift' command with the runner project root (D:/qontinui-root/qontinui-runner). It scans source files for useUIElement({ id: '...' }) registrations and compares them against assertion target IDs in all loaded .spec.uibridge.json files. The resulting DriftReport has two lists: missing_from_spec (elements in code but not in specs) and orphans_in_spec (assertion targets not matching any useUIElement registration). Results are shown in a modal with suggested assertion JSON for copy-paste.

assertions.description: A 'Check Drift' button (or similar label from SpecDriftButton) is visible in the connection bar

Clicking 'Check Drift' scans the runner source tree and shows a modal with two sections: 'Missing from spec' (element IDs in useUIElement registrations that have no matching assertion target) and 'Orphans in spec' (assertion targets with no matching useUIElement in the source). Each missing entry includes suggested assertion JSON for copy-paste. An empty report means perfect spec-code sync.

groups.name: Compile State Machine
groups.description: The 'Compile State Machine' button (violet Network icon, id=specs-btn-compile-sm) compiles the stateMachine sections from all loaded .spec.uibridge.json files into a single runtime state machine via compileStateMachineFromSpecs(). It then persists the result to the backend DB via persistCompiledStateMachine() and loads it into the UI Bridge engine so the pathfinder can navigate by state ID. Specs without a stateMachine section are skipped. This is distinct from the State Machine page's 'Generate for Runner' which reverse-engineers from React source.

assertions.description: Clicking 'Compile State Machine' aggregates all stateMachine.states arrays from loaded page specs, merges them into a single compiled state machine, persists it to the backend DB, and loads it into the UI Bridge engine. On success the compiled state machine is queryable for automated navigation. On error the failure is logged to console. The button is disabled when no specs are loaded.
assertions.precondition: At least one spec with a stateMachine section is loaded

assertions.description: The compiled state machine is the runtime artifact used by the UI Bridge pathfinder for page navigation. Each state in the compiled machine corresponds to a distinct UI configuration from a loaded spec's stateMachine.states entry. States from multiple specs are merged into a single global machine — meaning state IDs must be unique across specs. The compilation is the canonical way to update the pathfinder from spec changes.

groups.name: File Loading and Saving
groups.description: Specs can be loaded from and saved to disk via Tauri file dialogs. Loading supports six extensions: .spec.uibridge.json (page-spec), .architecture.uibridge.json, .api.uibridge.json, .data.uibridge.json, .deps.uibridge.json, .constraints.uibridge.json. Kind detection is from filename extension first, then content structure (groups array → page-spec, endpoints → api, entities → data, modules → dependency, budgets/techStack → constraint/architecture). Loaded file specs appear under 'File' in the tree and are auto-selected. Saving exports the config as indented JSON with the correct extension.

assertions.description: When loading a spec file, the kind is detected from the filename extension first. If ambiguous, the JSON content is inspected: a top-level 'groups' array → page-spec; 'endpoints' → api; 'entities' → data; 'modules' → dependency; 'budgets' or 'performanceBudgets' → constraint; 'techStack' → architecture. The wrong kind causes the wrong overview component to render.

After a file is loaded, it is automatically added to the tree under the 'File' app group, the spec node is selected and highlighted, and (for page-specs with groups) the node is expanded. The center panel immediately shows the loaded spec's details without requiring a manual click.

When 'Save' is clicked, the Tauri save dialog suggests a filename using the spec's ID with the correct extension for its kind (e.g., 'runner:specs.spec.uibridge.json' for page-spec). The saved file contains the spec config serialized as formatted JSON (2-space indent).
assertions.precondition: Any spec is selected

groups.name: AI Spec-Brief Toggle
groups.description: The 'Generate with AI (spec brief)' switch (id=specs-ai-toggle, role=switch) controls which pipeline runs when 'Build Workflow' is clicked. On by default (aria-pressed=true, fuchsia). Off state (aria-pressed=false, muted) routes to deterministic buildSpecWorkflow(). State persists via instanceStorage key 'specs.useAiGeneration'. The Sparkles icon always shows regardless of state.

assertions.description: On first load with no persisted preference, the specs-ai-toggle switch has aria-pressed=true (fuchsia styling), indicating the AI pipeline is on by default

Clicking specs-ai-toggle flips aria-pressed between true and false and persists the new value via instanceStorage key 'specs.useAiGeneration'. Visual style switches between fuchsia background (on) and muted/transparent (off). The change takes effect immediately — the next 'Build Workflow' click uses the newly selected pipeline.

When the AI pipeline is triggered, the 'Build Workflow' button immediately shows a Loader2 spinner and 'Generating…' text and is disabled. It stays disabled until the pipeline completes (success or error). On error, the button returns to 'Build Workflow' with the Hammer icon and enabled state; no error message is shown to the user (error is logged to console).
assertions.precondition: AI toggle is on and Build Workflow was clicked with a spec selected

states.name: Empty — No Specs Loaded
states.description: No specs have been loaded. The spec tree shows 'No specs loaded.' with guidance. The detail panel shows GlobalIssuesPanel. Mode badge shows 'viewer'.

transitions.name: Load bundled specs
transitions.description: Click Bundled to load all bundled specs from the registry

transitions.name: Start app discovery
transitions.description: Click Discover to connect to a running app

states.name: Discovering — Connecting to App
states.description: Discovery is in flight. The connection status row shows a cyan Loader2 spinner and 'Connecting…'.

states.name: Specs Loaded — No Selection
states.description: Specs are visible in the tree grouped by app. No spec is selected. Mode badge shows 'viewer'. Detail panel shows GlobalIssuesPanel.

transitions.name: Click a spec node in the tree

states.name: Spec Selected — Viewer Mode
states.description: A spec is selected. Center panel shows spec details: for page-spec, the tabbed view (Assertions/Issues/Triage) with Assertions active; for other types, specialized overviews. Mode badge shows 'viewer'. Save and Build Workflow buttons are visible. For page-specs, the Edit button is also visible.

states.name: Spec Selected — Editor Mode
states.description: A page-spec is selected with edit mode active. Mode badge shows 'editor'. 'Done' button replaces 'Edit' with amber styling. Spec overview shows groups with trash icons and 'Add group' area.

transitions.name: Select a group while in edit mode

states.name: Group Selected — Viewer Mode
states.description: A group within a page-spec is selected. Center panel shows GroupDetail: group name heading with category badge, description, and assertion rows. Mode badge shows 'viewer'. Eye icons and type badges are read-only.

states.name: Group Selected — Editor Mode
states.description: A group is selected with edit mode active. Assertion rows show clickable eye icons and trash icons. 'Add assertion' button visible at the bottom. Mode badge shows 'editor'. Done button visible.

transitions.name: Click the parent spec node while in edit mode

states.name: Issues Tab Active
states.description: The Issues tab is selected for a page-spec. SpecIssuesPanel renders showing known issues filtered by specId and pageUrl.

states.name: Triage Tab Active
states.description: The Triage tab is selected for a page-spec. SpecTriageView renders for regression triage.

states.name: AI Chat — Review Mode
states.description: Review mode is active in the AI chat panel. Quick-action buttons visible: 'Review spec quality', 'Find gaps', 'Suggest improvements', 'Generate assertions'. For page-specs: 'Build verification workflow' also present.

states.name: AI Chat — Create Mode
states.description: Create mode is active in the AI chat panel. Template buttons visible: 'New Page Spec', 'New Architecture Spec', 'New API Spec', 'New Data Spec'. Input placeholder says 'Describe the spec you want to create…'.

states.name: Contracts View
states.description: View mode is 'Contracts'. ContractBuilder replaces the three-panel editor. The 'Contracts' header button has zinc-700 highlight styling.

states.name: Experimentation View
states.description: View mode is 'Experimentation'. SpecExperimentationDashboard renders with tabs: Compliance, Accuracy, Coverage, Consistency, Freshness. The 'Experimentation' header button has zinc-700 highlight.
